# KMAC Entropy Generation Module Specification

## 1. Overview

This module provides pseudo-random data for masking operations inside the KMAC hashing datapath. It can obtain entropy from one of two sources:

- an Entropy Distribution Network (EDN), which supplies one 32-bit word per transfer;
- software-written seed words.

The module generates an 800-bit random value for masking logic, and a separate message-mask value used to mask the message datapath. It also tracks completed key-block hashing operations and can use that count to trigger an entropy refresh.

The module shall operate as a deterministic pseudo-random generator after being seeded. Its security depends on the quality of the supplied seed entropy.

## 2. Initialization and Mode Selection

After reset, the module shall be in its reset state. If software has not yet enabled the entropy module, the module shall assert its random-valid output using the current generator contents as placeholder data. This prevents dependent logic from being blocked before software has configured entropy.

When software asserts the entropy-ready enable, the module shall:

- clear any placeholder random valid output;
- capture the current entropy mode;
- begin the sequence corresponding to that mode.

If the captured mode is neither software-seed mode nor EDN mode, the module shall generate an “invalid entropy mode” error and enter an error-wait state.

The entropy mode shall be captured at the moment the entropy-ready enable is asserted. Changes to the mode after that point shall not take effect until the module returns to its reset state.

## 3. Software-Seed Mode

In software-seed mode, the module shall not issue requests to EDN.

After the entropy-ready enable is asserted, the module shall wait for software to supply seed words. A complete initialization requires five 32-bit seed words. Software shall supply these words one at a time, in ascending index order.

The module shall use each supplied seed word to update its internal generator state. After the fifth and final seed word is accepted, the module shall:

- generate an initial random value;
- assert the random-valid output;
- enter normal operation.

In software-seed mode, seed words are consumed only during this initialization sequence. Later software seed updates shall be ignored.

The module shall never mix entropy sources. When operating in software-seed mode, EDN data shall not be used.

## 4. EDN Mode

In EDN mode, the module shall request entropy from EDN whenever a reseed is required. A reseed is required:

- during initialization after reset;
- when software requests an entropy refresh;
- in EDN mode, when the hash operation threshold is reached.

The module shall assert its EDN request and keep it asserted until the full reseed has been received or the wait timer expires.

A complete reseed from EDN requires five 32-bit words. Each EDN transfer provides one word. When the final word of a reseed is received, the module shall:

- deassert the EDN request;
- generate a fresh random value;
- assert the random-valid output.

If the current random value is consumed while a reseed is in progress, the module shall clear the random-valid output and continue waiting for the reseed to complete.

### 4.1 EDN Wait Timer

The module has a programmable wait timer with a prescaler and a limit value. A limit value of zero disables the timeout.

The timer shall run while an EDN reseed is outstanding. If the timer expires before the full reseed is received, the module shall:

- cancel the outstanding EDN request;
- report a “wait timer expired” error;
- enter an error-wait state.

While in this error-wait state, the module shall keep the random-valid output asserted so that an ongoing hashing operation can complete.

## 5. Random Value Output Behavior

The module shall provide an 800-bit pseudo-random output. This output is meaningful only when the random-valid output is asserted.

The module shall also provide an early output that indicates, one cycle in advance, that a newly generated random value will become valid on the following cycle.

In normal ready-state operation:

- After a new random value has been generated, the module shall keep the random-valid output asserted across two consumption events.
- After the first consumption event, the module shall not deassert the valid output.
- After the second consumption event, the module shall deassert the valid output and advance the generator to create the next random value.

This behavior applies when:

- fast-processing mode is disabled; or
- fast-processing mode is enabled and a key-block operation is being processed.

### 5.1 Fast-Processing Mode

When fast-processing mode is enabled and no key-block operation is being processed, the module shall not respond to consumption events by deasserting valid or generating a new value. Instead, it shall keep the current random-valid output asserted indefinitely as placeholder data.

When fast-processing mode is enabled and a key-block operation is being processed, the module shall behave normally and refresh the random data on the required consumption pattern.

## 6. Message Mask Output

The module shall provide a message-mask output derived from the same pseudo-random generator state used for the random value output.

When message masking is enabled, the generator shall advance every clock cycle, and the message-mask output shall be updated every clock cycle.

When message masking is disabled, the message-mask output shall retain its current value except when the generator advances for random-value generation.

## 7. Hash Operation Counter

The module shall count completed key-block hashing operations. An operation is counted when the key-block processing indication transitions from active to inactive.

The counter shall:

- start from zero after reset;
- increment on each completed key-block operation;
- be cleared when software asserts the hash-counter clear request;
- be cleared when an entropy refresh is requested;
- be cleared when the hash threshold is reached.

If a nonzero hash threshold is configured, the module shall detect when the counter reaches or exceeds that threshold. Upon detection:

- the counter shall be cleared;
- in EDN mode, an entropy reseed shall be initiated;
- the internal threshold condition shall be cleared when that EDN reseed begins.

If the hash threshold is zero, threshold detection shall be disabled.

When software requests an entropy refresh:

- the hash counter shall be cleared;
- in EDN mode, the module shall start a reseed;
- in software-seed mode, no entropy source switch shall occur.

## 8. Error Behavior

The module shall report errors through an error output with an error code.

The module shall report:

- an invalid entropy mode error when the entropy-ready enable is asserted while the captured mode is neither software-seed nor EDN;
- a wait-timer-expired error when the EDN wait timer expires before a reseed completes.

When one of these errors is recognized, the module shall:

- assert the error output with the corresponding code;
- enter an error-wait state;
- stop issuing EDN requests;
- stop accepting new reseed activity;
- keep the random-valid output asserted so current hashing can finish.

The module shall remain in the error-wait state until software asserts the error-processed indication. When that occurs, the module shall return to its reset state. If the entropy-ready enable is still asserted at that time, the module shall immediately begin initialization again using the current mode.

## 9. Integrity and Life-Cycle Escalation

If an internal counter integrity check fails, the module shall assert a counter-error flag.

If the control logic enters an illegal state, or if the life-cycle escalation indication is active, the module shall:

- enter a terminal error state;
- assert the control-error flag;
- stop all normal generation, reseeding, and request activity;
- remain in that state until reset.

Life-cycle escalation shall override all other operating behavior.

## 10. Reset Behavior

On reset, the module shall clear counters, error flags, request outputs, and active state. The random-valid output shall then be asserted only as placeholder data if software has not yet enabled entropy, as described in Section 2.
